corrected_draft.description_long: An SEC Schedule 13D amendment filed by Vivek Ramaswamy and other reporting persons states that he beneficially owned 5,693,897 Strive, Inc. shares, representing 8.4% of the class under the filing’s stated assumption that Class B shares convert to Class A. It explains that Strive’s at-the-market share sales increased the number of outstanding shares, causing the reporting group to fall below the 50% voting-power threshold in its shareholder agreement. The agreement then terminated automatically, and the reporting persons ceased to constitute a group. The amendment says Ramaswamy still beneficially owned more than 5% and would report separately; the other exiting persons fell below 5%. This establishes an ownership disclosure and reporting change. DOJ described the complaint as its latest action against what it called unlawful judicial overreach. corrected_draft.description_short: Vance defends Trump's fake Kharg attack videos as sending Iran a message

corrected_draft.description_long: Reuters reported on August 31, 2026, that Vice President JD Vance defended a social-media post by President Donald Trump showing AI-generated explosions associated with Iran's Kharg Island. Vance characterized the post as a message to Iran rather than an announcement that a military attack had occurred. The timing was notable: Reuters said his explanation came one day after Trump posted the imagery. The supplied account states that the depicted explosions did not represent a real attack on Kharg Island. corrected_draft.title: Trump exaggerates border-wall construction and cashless-bail outcomes at convention
corrected_draft.description_short: Trump exaggerates border-wall construction and cashless-bail outcomes at convention
corrected_draft.description_medium: At the Republican midterm convention in Dallas on September 10, 2026, Trump claimed he had built almost 2,000 miles of border wall and warned that under no-cash-bail policies, people accused of murder could be released within hours. FactCheck.org reported that total construction across his two terms was 674 miles, including replacement barriers, and that release of murder suspects without cash bail is exceedingly rare where permitted.
corrected_draft.description_long: During his September 10, 2026, remarks at the Republican midterm convention in Dallas, Donald Trump claimed, “I built almost 2,000 miles of wall.” He also argued against no-cash-bail policies by saying that someone who kills another person could be “out in the streets two hours later.” FactCheck.org examined both claims in its review of the convention’s second night. The fact-check reported that 674 miles of border-wall system had been built across Trump’s two terms when replacement and secondary barriers are counted, while 124 miles were built where no barrier had previously existed. Thus the “almost 2,000 miles” figure greatly overstated construction. On bail, FactCheck.org noted that some states retain exceptions for violent crimes and murder, and that release of a murder suspect without cash bail is possible only in some jurisdictions and exceedingly rare. This record concerns claims made in a speech and the fact-check’s comparison; it does not describe a new wall project or a uniform national bail rule.
